question: Can a fixed language host and connector use a separately trained module with different world rules?
organ_meaning: An analogy for an internal part with a different job. An energy module scores possible next states; energy here is a learned score, not electrical power.

established_precedents.title: LLM Augmented LLMs: Expanding Capabilities through Composition (CALM)
established_precedents.summary: CALM trains a connection between intermediate representations of two frozen language models.
established_precedents.limit: This is model composition, not proof that arbitrary modules can be exchanged without further training.

established_precedents.title: V-JEPA 2: Self-Supervised Video Models Enable Understanding, Prediction and Planning
established_precedents.summary: V-JEPA 2 predicts future representations and uses them for planning. Its language alignment also uses a trained connection.
established_precedents.limit: Predictive video representations do not automatically form a working language-model module.

established_precedents.title: Off-Manifold Refinement: Guiding Video Generators with a Frozen World Model
established_precedents.summary: Off-Manifold Refinement trains an adapter that lets a frozen world model guide a frozen video generator during generation.
established_precedents.limit: The demonstration concerns video generation, not a language-model organ transplant.

established_precedents.title: the Mouth is Not the Brain: Bridging Energy-Based World Models and Language Generation
established_precedents.author: Junichiro Niimi
established_precedents.summary: Niimi links a Deep Boltzmann Machine to frozen GPT-2 through a trained soft-prompt adapter. It generates reviews, not temporal state predictions. Replacing either model requires adapter retraining. Time-series modeling remains future work.

current_development: The same-recipe second attempt completed and failed its original learning requirement. All four learned rule modules passed all 24 of 24 local transitions, but the host plus connector and the comparison model did not meet the training-task requirements. The first interrupted attempt remains closed.
development_limit: Integrity-audit PASS confirms the records and calculations, not task success. These four development worlds were already used in training; no unseen-rule transplant or general architecture comparison was established. Failure to access or use the rules remains to be distinguished.
transformation: Reviewed primary-paper context and terminal development facts, including the separate retrospective writer recovery. Original stopped-run history and all earlier failures remain preserved. No raw model outputs copied.
latest_diagnostic: A completed fixed-weight check passed all required controls. Forcing access to the relevant whole rule row gave 10 of 96 correct choices, compared with 16 normally. None of 96 pairs followed both selected rules. Every forced setting changed the delivered signal.
diagnostic_limit: The same four training worlds and one-action questions were reused. Whole-row forcing can change signal strength and the kind of input seen during training; earlier positions retain normal memory. No cause of the original learning failure, unseen-rule transfer or novelty is established.
latest_address_reader: A new offline supervised reader passed on 16 fitted combinations and 8 combinations excluded from the fit, with no state, action or joint address errors or ties. It used saved host vectors and made no new model calls.
address_reader_limit: All 24 questions use one template and were already exposed during development. Four identical world copies were collapsed before the split. This FP64 reader is separate from the failed connector and has not been installed live. It establishes no answer writing, composition, unseen-rule transfer, original-failure cause or novelty.
next_step: Prospectively check the fixed reader on live host signals. Only after that separate admission should a fixed one-step assembly be reviewed. No automatic launch.
latest_writer_attempt: Historical original attempt: stopped on 5 October at 16:26 UTC because the audit rejected normal model-cache links. No behavioral result existed at that stop. The original STOP and public stop summary remain unchanged.
writer_stop_limit: The original run never completed its audit. A metadata follow-up alone did not grade scores. The later result is in a separate disclosed retrospective recovery, not an original-protocol completion.
latest_writer_recovery: A separate retrospective audit passed the unchanged complete checker and all original writer gates: 128/128 fitted-context choices, 128/128 fit-excluded-context choices and 768/768 cached-organ-vector compatibility cells, with zero ties. A separate recount agreed. No model calls, updates or refits were repeated.
writer_recovery_limit: An 8,192-weight writer ranks an explicitly supplied answer among eight candidates. All data were development-exposed. Its 448 label pairs reuse 128 choices. Cached probabilities are not an executed energy transplant; the offline reader remains uninstalled and unjoined. No generation, calibrated probabilities, reasoning, new rules or novelty is established. Changed architecture, supervision and optimization prevent attributing the old bridge failure to one cause.
later_mechanistic_question: After a fixed-interface swap to an independently learned new-rule module, does an intermediate host state causally determine the next rule query? An external controller doing the rollout would answer a different question.
